tension: This is not an obstacle. It is an invitation that the traveller did not accept.
traveller_stance: Does not enter. Finds the way around.

npc_attitude: In the canopy above — eyes. Eight of them, arranged in two rows, reflecting the light from between the leaves.
concrete_content: It is not moving. It registered the traveller's presence some time before the traveller registered its. It is waiting to see if the traveller will stop.
tension: Stopping is the wrong answer. Stopping means it has time to drop.
traveller_stance: Does not stop. Does not look up directly. Moves at a pace that says: aware but not afraid.

npc_attitude: The tree directly above has too much stillness in it — no movement even in a light wind, every branch weighted down by something that is not leaves.
concrete_content: It is one spider or it is several, and they have been there long enough to stop the tree moving. The weight of them is visible in how the branches sit.
tension: It — or they — have been watching the approach for several minutes.
traveller_stance: Does not stop under the tree. Does not look up. Keeps moving.

npc_attitude: A stone post at the junction — plain iron-grey, four feet tall, unremarkable. Except it was not there on the way in.
concrete_content: It has no inscription. It has no obvious purpose. It is positioned exactly at the center of the junction, equidistant from all three paths.
tension: It moved. Between when the traveller entered the valley and now, it moved here.
traveller_stance: Studies it without approaching. Takes the western path. Does not go back the way it came.

npc_attitude: Among the carved stones at the forest edge — one that looks like the others until the light changes and it doesn't.
concrete_content: The shadows fall wrong on this one. The proportions are almost right but the stone's grain doesn't match the carvings around it. It is newer, or it is different, or it is not stone.
tension: The Woses placed these carvings for a reason. Whatever this one is, it is not their work.
traveller_stance: Does not touch it. Does not get closer. Leaves the forest edge.

npc_attitude: The stone figure at the path's edge has turned since the traveller last passed it.
concrete_content: It was facing east. It is now facing the traveller. The base has not moved — only the figure, from the waist up. It is watching.
tension: It has not attacked. The constructs do not attack unless the boundary is crossed. The question is where the boundary is.
traveller_stance: Does not cross the path. Goes around.

npc_attitude: There are more of them than there were. The path that had three guardian-stones now has seven. Three of the new ones have no moss, no weathering.
concrete_content: They are closing in incrementally. The path is being narrowed. Whatever the boundary was, the traveller has been moving inside it and the constructs are adjusting.
tension: The Woses who made these are somewhere close, watching through the constructs' awareness.
traveller_stance: Stops. Addresses the forest directly. Says: I mean no harm to this wood. Then waits.

npc_attitude: One sitting on a boulder at the road-side, eating something it would be better not to identify. It looks up when the traveller passes.
concrete_content: It says — slowly, with the effort of someone who doesn't use speech often — that the traveller is small. It says this as an observation, not as a threat. It is genuinely noting the size.
tension: The observation has no follow-up. It goes back to what it was eating.
traveller_stance: Agrees that yes, it is small. Continues.

npc_attitude: It comes out of a cave-mouth at the bend and stops when it sees the traveller. It did not expect company.
concrete_content: It says: you're not supposed to be on this road. It says it with the specific confusion of something following instructions it doesn't fully understand. Someone told it the road would be clear.
tension: Someone gave it instructions. Someone expected the road to be clear. The traveller is the problem in that plan.
traveller_stance: Asks who said the road would be clear. Watches it decide whether to answer.

npc_attitude: A barrow-entrance, and in front of it a figure that occupies the threshold — not blocking it, being it.
concrete_content: It does not speak first. It is the threshold. Whatever is in the barrow behind it is what it was in life, and it has been in that barrow a long time.
tension: It will not move. It cannot move. It is bound to this place in a way that is complete.
traveller_stance: Does not approach. Addresses it from outside the barrow's influence. Asks its name.

npc_attitude: It is on the road. Not beside it — on it. Standing in the middle, occupying the center, facing the traveller's direction.
concrete_content: It is not one of the mindless ones. Its eyes track. It has something it wants to say, or something it wants to do, and it has been waiting on this road for the right person.
tension: The traveller may or may not be the right person. It is making that determination now.
traveller_stance: Stops. Does not approach. Lets it make its determination without interference.

npc_attitude: It appears at dusk — not suddenly, just present where it was not. Standing at the edge of the road, looking at the traveller's fire.
concrete_content: It remembers fire. The memory is old and the connection between the memory and the fire is broken in ways it cannot articulate. It looks at the fire the way the very old look at things that remind them of something they cannot name.
tension: It is not threatening. It is homesick for something it can no longer reach.
traveller_stance: Does not invite it closer. Does not drive it away. Lets it stand there.

npc_attitude: It speaks before the traveller sees it — from behind, already close.
concrete_content: It says a name. Not the traveller's name. Someone else's name, spoken with the particular urgency of the long-dead looking for someone who has also long since died.
tension: It will not stop until it understands that the person it is looking for is gone. That understanding may take a long time to arrive.
traveller_stance: Turns to face it. Says: that person is dead. Says it clearly. Waits to see if it can receive this.

npc_attitude: A creak from above — not wood settling, deliberate. The tree has something to say and this is how it begins.
concrete_content: It says, after a long pause, that this path has been used more often recently. It says this with the interest of something that has been watching the same stretch of ground for four hundred years and noticed a change.
tension: The change it noticed is recent enough to be meaningful. It is asking, in the way Ents ask, whether the traveller knows what is causing it.
traveller_stance: Tells it what the road has looked like from ground-level. Takes the time the answer deserves.

npc_attitude: It steps onto the path from the treeline — the motion takes approximately forty seconds and the sound of it is the sound of the forest rearranging itself.
concrete_content: It says that something has been entering the forest from the east for several nights and that it smells wrong in a way the Ent does not have precise language for. It says: wrong in the way the forest was wrong in the second age, before we understood what was happening.
tension: An Ent saying this is not hyperbole. It has comparative data spanning thousands of years.
traveller_stance: Asks it: what does wrong smell like, specifically? What did it smell like in the second age?

npc_attitude: A flooded section of the road ahead — shallow enough to wade but the current pulls sideways.
concrete_content: The ford here is normally reliable. Something upstream has changed the drainage. The far bank is firm.
tension: A minor cost of time and wet boots, nothing more. The road continues beyond it unchanged.
traveller_stance: Finds the shallowest crossing. Wades.

npc_attitude: A section of cliff-face above the road shows fresh scoring — recent rockfall, the debris still white against the older stone.
concrete_content: The fall happened within the last day. Loose material still hangs on the upper face. The debris field across the road is passable but the passage under the unstable rock is perhaps thirty metres.
tension: The risk is real but brief. The alternative is a long detour.
traveller_stance: Crosses fast, under the overhang, without stopping.

npc_attitude: A section of the road has subsided — not collapsed, sunk, the surface intact but the ground beneath it no longer solid.
concrete_content: The subsidence is several metres across. The surface holds weight for now. Something underground has changed — water, rot, a cavity. It will not hold indefinitely.
tension: The road is still technically passable. The word technically is doing a great deal of work.
traveller_stance: Tests the edge with a stick. Crosses close to the high side where the ground is more solid.

npc_attitude: A tree across the road — freshly fallen, root-ball still tearing free of the soil on the uphill side.
concrete_content: It came down in the last few hours. The crown is thick and tangled; going over it is possible but slow. Going around it on the uphill side means climbing the root-ball, which is unstable.
tension: Neither route is dangerous, only awkward. The road is clear on the far side.
traveller_stance: Goes around the root-ball on the lower side where the ground is firmer.

npc_attitude: A bog has encroached onto the road — the surface looks firm but the footprint sinks two inches on the first step.
concrete_content: The bog extends perhaps fifty metres. The road skirts the edge of it but the road itself is compromised. Deeper in, the ground is black water with a grass skin over it.
tension: People have crossed here before — there are marks on the verge where travelers pushed through. The marks are old.
traveller_stance: Tests each step. Moves to the verge when the road softens. Takes twice the time.

npc_attitude: The bridge is out — not collapsed, removed. The timbers are gone and only the stone piers stand in the river.
concrete_content: The river here is not crossable on foot. The nearest ford is a full half-day upstream. Someone removed those timbers deliberately.
tension: Who removes a bridge and why is the question. The answer is somewhere upstream near the ford.
traveller_stance: Does not cross. Turns upstream. Moves carefully.

npc_attitude: The ledge-path crumbles underfoot — a section approximately two metres gives way without warning.
concrete_content: One foot goes through. The drop below is not fatal but the recovery requires immediate action — push back, redistribute weight, find the solid edge.
tension: Two seconds of real danger, then it is past. The path is narrower on the other side of the gap.
traveller_stance: Pushes back hard. Finds the solid edge. Does not look down. Continues.

npc_attitude: Flash of movement and a loud crack — a branch the width of an arm falls from directly above, misses by less than a foot.
concrete_content: The dead wood was sitting in the canopy. Something — wind, a bird, nothing visible — dislodged it. The impact crater in the soil beside the path is considerable.
tension: Nothing to be done about it. It either hits or it doesn't.
traveller_stance: Moves out from under the canopy. Keeps moving.

npc_attitude: The ground opens — a sinkhole, perhaps two metres across, directly in the path. The near edge crumbles inward as the traveller stops.
concrete_content: The hole is deep enough that the bottom isn't visible. The soil around it is still settling. It opened within the last hour — the broken turf edges are fresh.
tension: The path is gone here. The way around requires going fifty metres off-track into steep ground.
traveller_stance: Steps back from the crumbling edge. Goes around. Does not hurry — the ground here is clearly not reliable.

npc_attitude: Fresh deer-slots in the soft ground beside the path — a doe and two young, moving toward the stream.
concrete_content: Made within a few hours, heading downhill. The slots are clean and unworried — no sign of flight. The deer have not been alarmed recently.
tension: Deer moving calmly means the forest ahead is quiet. That is worth knowing.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction. Continues.

npc_attitude: The ground around a waterhole has been heavily churned — large hooves, many animals, recently.
concrete_content: A herd came through here within the last day. The mud is still wet. Whatever brought them here in numbers — a long dry spell, or something drove them off their usual ground.
tension: Driven animals mean something was behind them. The direction they came from is worth noting.
traveller_stance: Reads the direction of the herd's arrival. Considers what was behind them.

npc_attitude: The carcass of a large elk, untouched. Not killed — starved, recently, in a region where starving elk make no sense.
concrete_content: The body is intact, no predator-sign, no disease-sign. It simply stopped and did not move again. The grass around it is ungrazed.
tension: Herbivores do not starve in good country in this season unless something has made them too frightened to graze.
traveller_stance: Studies the ground. Notes the direction the elk was facing when it stopped. Continues with the ridge on one side.

npc_attitude: A herd on the hillside above the road — moving uphill in the late afternoon, which is the right direction at this hour.
concrete_content: Thirty or forty animals, the usual mixed herd. Moving at a natural pace, no sign of disturbance.
tension: The land up there is good. Nothing has disturbed it today.
traveller_stance: Notes the count. Continues.

npc_attitude: A large solitary animal on the skyline — not a deer. Too large, wrong proportions, standing still on the ridge.
concrete_content: An aurochs, or a giant breed the traveller has not seen before. It is watching the road below. It does not move.
tension: Animals that watch roads from ridges without moving are worth taking note of. This one is not afraid of the road.
traveller_stance: Notes the size and direction. Keeps moving.

npc_attitude: A herd grazing the meadow beside the road — unperturbed, heads down, moving slowly in the late morning light.
concrete_content: Perhaps twenty animals. They registered the traveller's approach and decided the traveller was not interesting.
tension: The herd being calm means the road ahead has been undisturbed. Frightened animals do not return quickly to a feeding ground.
traveller_stance: Passes without disturbing them. Uses the observation.

npc_attitude: A stag at the water's edge, drinking. It looks up when the traveller approaches, holds for a long moment, then retreats into the trees without urgency.
concrete_content: It held long enough to assess. The assessment came back: not a threat. That assessment has been running correctly for this animal so far.
tension: Nothing alarmed it before the traveller arrived. The forest behind it was quiet.
traveller_stance: Notes the calm. Continues.

npc_attitude: The herd at the meadow-edge scatters as the traveller rounds the bend — not in panic, in the unhurried retreat of animals that are startled but not truly frightened.
concrete_content: They move uphill and stop at the treeline to look back. A normal response. They will return within the hour.
tension: Nothing else spooked them. This was the traveller.
traveller_stance: Continues without pursuing them.

npc_attitude: A boar on the path ahead — huge, old, scarred. It faces the traveller for a full three seconds, then turns and crashes into the undergrowth.
concrete_content: It chose to leave. That is unusual for a boar this size. Something on the traveller read as more dangerous than a large boar was willing to deal with.
tension: The shadow, perhaps. Or something that the boar could smell that the traveller cannot name.
traveller_stance: Notes the encounter. Continues. Wonders what the boar smelled.

npc_attitude: Wolf-prints crossing the path — a pair, moving at a trot, heading north. Made last night.
concrete_content: Both adults, by the size. Not a pack, a bonded pair. Moving purposefully, not hunting — the stride is too regular for active hunting.
tension: They have a destination. The direction is north, same as the traveller.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction. Checks behind. Continues.

npc_attitude: The remains of a kill on the road — bones, hide, scattered. Something large fed here recently.
concrete_content: The kill is clean-stripped in the way of bears, not wolves or cats. The bones are crushed. The hide is turned inside-out, which bears do systematically.
tension: A bear large enough to turn a deer's hide inside-out and crush the long bones is significantly larger than average.
traveller_stance: Reads the size from the print-depth in the mud beside the kill. Continues. Keeps the road open on both sides.

npc_attitude: Claw-marks on a tree beside the path at head height — five parallel gouges, deep, in hardwood.
concrete_content: Marking territory. The height means the animal stood on its hind legs to make them — eight feet minimum. The marks are recent enough that the wood inside the gouges is still pale.
tension: Something very large is marking this path as its territory. The marks face the direction of travel.
traveller_stance: Does not touch the marks. Continues. Moves quietly.

npc_attitude: Something is following. Not seen, not heard — felt. The specific quality of being tracked by something that knows how to stay out of sight.
concrete_content: It has been there for perhaps twenty minutes. It matches pace changes. It does not come closer, but the distance between them has not increased either.
tension: Whatever it is, it is waiting for something — a change in terrain, a moment of inattention, a decision to stop.
traveller_stance: Does not stop. Does not look back directly. Moves onto open ground where the follower will have to cross open space to close the distance.

npc_attitude: Two of them, one on each side of the road. The one on the right is visible when it moves between trees. The one on the left is inferred from the behavior of the first.
concrete_content: They are coordinating. The one on the right is the visible element — the one that makes the prey watch right. The one on the left will move when the prey is watching right.
tension: This is a practiced technique. These animals have done this before.
traveller_stance: Does not watch right. Moves to the center of the road. Increases pace.

npc_attitude: The ruins of a small tower at the road's junction — foundation stones clear, the upper work long fallen.
concrete_content: Dunedain-built, by the cut of the remaining stones. Three hundred years old at minimum. The road junction it guarded still functions. The tower no longer does.
tension: The road has outlasted the people who built the tower to protect it. That is not unusual in the north.
traveller_stance: Notes the stonework. Takes the right fork.

npc_attitude: A village — inhabited, smoke from chimneys, faces at windows — but the gate is shut and nobody comes out.
concrete_content: The gate is new. The bar is heavy. The faces at the windows are watching the traveller in the specific way of people who have decided to wait and see.
tension: Something happened here recently. The caution is fresh.
traveller_stance: Does not approach the gate. Continues on the road past the village. Watches the faces watch.

npc_attitude: The village is empty. Not abandoned-empty — fled-empty. Doors open, fires cold, food left on tables.
concrete_content: Everything suggests speed. Animals are still in the paddocks, which means they left on foot and in a hurry.
tension: Whatever made them leave fast enough to leave the animals — it was visible, not rumoured.
traveller_stance: Does not enter. Notes the direction of the footprints leaving. Continues.

npc_attitude: A wayhouse at the road's edge — solid, maintained, with the universal signal of travelers' hospitality: a lit lamp in the window.
concrete_content: The fire inside is real and the food is basic and the bed is dry. The keeper asks no questions beyond which road the traveller came from, which is road-courtesy, not interrogation.
tension: A night spent here costs a small coin and restores something that cannot be easily named.
traveller_stance: Accepts the hospitality. Gives the road news owed in return.

npc_attitude: A farmstead off the road, the farmer visible in the yard, who raises a hand as the traveller passes.
concrete_content: The gesture is an invitation as much as a greeting — the way of the frontier, where hospitality is extended to travellers because travellers extend it in return.
tension: The farm has a barn. The barn is dry. The farmer has news from the eastern road that the traveller has not come from.
traveller_stance: Accepts the implied invitation. Spends an hour. Trades road news.

npc_attitude: A market at a crossroads — temporary, six or eight stalls, the kind that assembles on one specific day of the week.
concrete_content: Merchants from two directions. The goods tell the story of where they have been: northern furs beside southern cloth, which means both roads are open.
tension: Open roads and working markets mean the region is currently stable. That is worth knowing.
traveller_stance: Walks through. Reads the goods. Notes the roads that are represented.

npc_attitude: A fortified waystation with a small garrison — the gate is open and the guards are watching the road with professional attention.
concrete_content: The guards note the traveller. One of them moves to the gatepost but does not call out. The attention is heightened beyond normal duty.
tension: They are watching for something specific. The traveller does not match it.
traveller_stance: Returns the nod. Continues without stopping.

npc_attitude: The ruin watches. Not literally — but the way old places watch when their history is heavy enough to give them presence.
concrete_content: A keep that was besieged and taken and taken again and finally abandoned. The walls still hold. The gate-arch is intact. Nothing is inside except the weight of what happened there.
tension: It is not dangerous to stop here. It is uncomfortable in a way that has nothing to do with physical danger.
traveller_stance: Does not stop under the gate-arch. Passes it on the open side.

npc_attitude: The barrow-mound at the road's edge was not here before — or it was, but it was flat, and now the capstone has shifted and the opening is dark.
concrete_content: Someone opened it recently. The marks on the capstone are not old. The inside is dark and the air from it is cold in a way that has nothing to do with underground temperature.
tension: Things inside barrows do not open barrows from inside unless something has changed.
traveller_stance: Does not approach the opening. Notes the direction the capstone moved. Continues.

npc_attitude: The road through the settlement is closed — a rope across it and a man sitting beside the rope who does not look up when the traveller arrives.
concrete_content: He says, without looking up, that the road is closed until tomorrow morning. He does not explain why. He does not appear to be armed.
tension: The rope is a formality. The closure is not.
traveller_stance: Asks why. Gets: "town business." Takes the lane around.

npc_attitude: A natural overhang above a dry, flat floor — the kind of shelter that has been used for exactly this purpose for as long as travelers have used this road.
concrete_content: Old fire-rings, cleared ground, the beam of a previous traveler left notched against the wall as a hanger. Everything needed, nothing extra.
tension: Someone thought to leave the beam. It is still there. The traveller is glad of it.
traveller_stance: Sets up camp. Notes the road it is positioned to watch.

npc_attitude: A stand of medicinal herbs beside a spring — athelas among them, unmistakeable to those who know it.
concrete_content: The spring is clean and the herbs are well-established, which means this ground has not been poisoned or disturbed recently. A gift from the road.
tension: Taking a modest amount costs nothing. Leaving the plants rooted means they will be here for the next traveller.
traveller_stance: Harvests what can be spared. Drinks from the spring.

npc_attitude: A colony of beehives on the south-facing bank — tended hives, not wild, with the keeper's mark on the posts.
concrete_content: The keeper is not here but the hives are active and the marks are current. Someone is working these hives. The honey here is available for trade at whatever settlement owns the mark.
tension: Road knowledge: honey at the next settlement is fresh and reliable.
traveller_stance: Notes the keeper's mark. Continues.

npc_attitude: A fishery on the river — nets strung across a narrow, weirs directing the fish into a trapped pool. Nobody working it at this hour.
concrete_content: The equipment is good and well-maintained. The settlement that runs this fishery has enough people to do it properly and enough stability to maintain it across seasons.
tension: Stability in the settlements means the road is safe. This is indirect evidence but it is evidence.
traveller_stance: Notes the settlement's implied prosperity. Continues.

npc_attitude: A logging operation across the road — felled trunks being moved by a team of men and horses, the road temporarily blocked while they work.
concrete_content: The foreman sees the traveller and raises a hand: ten minutes. He means it.
tension: Normal commerce on a working road. The delay is genuine and brief.
traveller_stance: Waits at the edge of the work. Watches the operation.

npc_attitude: The road runs through a long meadow of wildflowers — unmanaged, brilliant, the kind that grows where no one has ploughed for a generation.
concrete_content: Cornflowers and poppies and things that have no common name in this part of the world. The contrast with the road-stone is absolute.
tension: A visual gift. Nothing else.
traveller_stance: Notes the colour. Continues.

npc_attitude: A dead zone — a stretch of fifty metres where nothing grows. The soil is dark and the ground is flat and the silence is the silence of absence.
concrete_content: No visible cause. The trees on either side are healthy. The ground here has no rock, no water problem. Something made it stop supporting life.
tension: Old battleground, perhaps. Or something was buried here. Or the shadow of something passed over it once and the ground remembers.
traveller_stance: Does not investigate. Passes through it quickly.

npc_attitude: A patch of Old Man's Beard covering a section of the treeline — the lichen that signals clean, wet air and old growth.
concrete_content: Old Man's Beard only grows in undisturbed forest with good air quality. Its presence here means this forest has been undisturbed for a long time.
tension: The forest ahead is old. Old forest has its own rules.
traveller_stance: Notes the lichen. Enters the forest accordingly.

npc_attitude: Thorny scrub has closed over the path — not a little, a wall of it, three metres high and clearly established over years.
concrete_content: The path has not been used in a long time. The scrub did not grow overnight. Someone stopped using this path and did not tell the map-makers.
tension: There is a reason this path was abandoned. It might be as simple as a better road was built. It might not.
traveller_stance: Does not force through the scrub. Looks for the reason the path was abandoned.

npc_attitude: The vegetation on both sides of the road has moved across it — not grown, moved. The stems are bent inward, not grown inward.
concrete_content: Something on the road is being closed off. The bending is recent — the stems are still green and supple where they cross the road surface.
tension: The Old Forest does this. Fangorn does this. If the traveller is in neither of those places, they should wonder what has learned to do it here.
traveller_stance: Cuts back the closing stems with a blade. Moves through. Does not linger.

npc_attitude: An ancient oak at the road's turning — a landmark, clearly, its trunk marked with generations of travellers' initials and the occasional waymark cut.
concrete_content: The oldest initials near the base are worn to illegibility. The tree was a waymark before writing was common in this region.
tension: It has been watching this junction for a very long time.
traveller_stance: Adds nothing to the marks. The tree has enough.

npc_attitude: The forest has changed — the canopy here is older and the trees are different in character. Not hostile, not welcoming. Simply ancient.
concrete_content: The oldest trees do not acknowledge travelers. They have been here too long to find travelers interesting. That is not the same as being safe here.
tension: Old trees have their own gravity. This section of forest pulls the road through it, not the other way.
traveller_stance: Walks without stopping. Does not disturb the undergrowth.

npc_attitude: The trees in this section are breathing — not literally, but the movement of air through them is patterned in a way that suggests something other than wind.
concrete_content: The rhythm is approximately twenty seconds. The movement is coordinated across trees that are not touching each other above ground.
tension: The roots are connected. What moves through one moves through all. The forest is aware of the traveller's passage in a way it has not been further back.
traveller_stance: Does not stop. Does not make noise. Passes through without meeting the rhythm.

npc_attitude: A root has heaved across the road — not a new root, an established one, which has lifted and moved to the surface since this section of road was last maintained.
concrete_content: The root is as thick as a torso and the road-stone has been pushed up on both sides of it. The crossing is awkward but manageable.
tension: The tree it belongs to is sixty feet back from the road. The root traveled a long way to get here.
traveller_stance: Steps over the root. Continues.

npc_attitude: The path through the forest has narrowed to nothing — not fallen trees, growing trees, their trunks moved close enough over years to close the gap.
concrete_content: This was a path once. The distance between the trunks was enough. Now it is not. The trees did not do this quickly.
tension: Old paths close for old reasons. The forest chose to close this one.
traveller_stance: Turns back. Finds the point where the path was still open. Chooses differently.

npc_attitude: Ravens in the canopy — not one or two, a gathering. The specific quality of raven noise that means something dead nearby, or something about to be.
concrete_content: They are calling to each other, not at the traveller. The subject of their interest is further along the road.
tension: Ravens know things. What they are gathered about is ahead.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction of their attention. Continues toward it with awareness up.

npc_attitude: A sound from above in the dark — not a bird in any normal category. Too large, the wingbeat wrong, the occasional sound between wingbeats suggesting a rider.
concrete_content: It is circling. The circle is centered approximately on the traveller's camp.
tension: Fell-beasts have riders. The rider can see in darkness better than the traveller can.
traveller_stance: Kills the fire. Does not move. Waits.

npc_attitude: Eagles above the pass — two of them, circling on the thermal above the high ground. Not hunting. Watching.
concrete_content: Great Eagles watch roads and passes with purpose. What they see they remember. What they decide to act on, they act on decisively.
tension: They have registered the traveller. The registration is neutral. So far.
traveller_stance: Continues. Does not make sudden movements.

npc_attitude: A murmuration of starlings over the marshland ahead — thousands of them, moving in coordinated sheets that bend and fold without colliding.
concrete_content: The murmuration is moving away from the direction the traveller is heading. Something in the marsh is driving them. Something changed there recently.
tension: Birds in mass flight tell the story of what is below them.
traveller_stance: Reads the direction of the murmuration's drift. Continues with that information.

npc_attitude: A hawk working the open ground beside the road — quartering back and forth in the systematic sweep of an active hunt.
concrete_content: It ignores the traveller completely. The hunt is genuine — it has a target below in the grass that the traveller cannot see.
tension: A hawk hunting means the field is quiet. Nothing larger has disturbed it recently.
traveller_stance: Notes the calm. Continues.

npc_attitude: A large owl from a hollow in the road-side tree — disturbed by the traveller's passing, it drops from the hollow and beats away into the forest.
concrete_content: Larger than expected. The wingspan clears four feet. It does not call, just leaves, which is owls.
tension: The hollow is empty now. The road is undisturbed.
traveller_stance: Watches it go. Continues.

npc_attitude: Otter-slides in the mud bank beside the river — two lanes worn smooth into the clay, angled into the water.
concrete_content: Active, recently used. The clay at the bottom of the slides is still wet. A family group, by the size difference between the tracks.
tension: Otters in good numbers mean the river is healthy — clean water, good fish, no upstream disruption.
traveller_stance: Notes the health of the river. Continues.

npc_attitude: Something large in the lake — a wake moving against the wind, no visible source, then gone.
concrete_content: The wake was V-shaped in the way of something swimming near the surface. The width of the V at its point suggests something perhaps eight to twelve feet long.
tension: The lake looks still again. The wake did not come toward the shore.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction it was moving. Does not swim in this lake.

npc_attitude: Beavers working a dam upstream of the ford — the sound of them carrying and placing timber audible from the road.
concrete_content: The dam is new. The pond behind it is expanding. The ford below it will be shallower for the next few weeks as the pond fills.
tension: Useful road knowledge: ford conditions changed upstream.
traveller_stance: Notes the new dam. Adjusts the ford expectation.

npc_attitude: The ford is blocked — not by water level, by crocodiles. Three of them, sun-bathing across the shallows in positions that make crossing impossible.
concrete_content: They are not aggressive — yet. They are using the ford because it is warm stone and shallow water, which suits them perfectly. They will not move willingly.
tension: Crocodiles at a ford are not a fight worth having. There is a boat crossing a mile downstream.
traveller_stance: Does not attempt the ford. Finds the boat crossing.

npc_attitude: The fish are gone from this stretch of river — not a hook-point to be found, the banks empty of birds, the water simply empty.
concrete_content: Fish do not leave a stretch of water without reason. Something in this section of river drives them away or feeds on them until they are gone.
tension: The emptiness is recent — the bird-droppings on the rocks show last week's activity, nothing this week.
traveller_stance: Does not fish here. Does not fill water from this stretch. Moves on.

npc_attitude: A shape under the surface of the deep pool at the river's bend — too large for any fish of this river, moving slowly along the bottom.
concrete_content: It turns at the pool's end and comes back. It has been doing this for some time — the silt at the bottom is disturbed in a regular pattern.
tension: Whatever it is, it is aware of the traveller at the bank. It has turned to parallel them each time they move.
traveller_stance: Does not enter the water. Moves away from the bank.

npc_attitude: The lake surface is still — completely still, in a wind that should be making it move.
concrete_content: The stillness is localized. Twenty metres out, where the water should be responding to the wind, it is flat and dark. Something below the surface is suppressing the movement.
tension: The Watcher in the Water is a name given to things like this. The name implies others have been watched from the same bank.
traveller_stance: Moves away from the lake's edge. Takes the high path.

npc_attitude: Snake-track in the dust of the road — sinuous, continuous, freshly made, crossing from the sunny verge to the shade under the opposite hedge.
concrete_content: Moving in the mid-morning means it is warming up. Large, by the track width — perhaps four feet of snake, minimum. Not hunting, just relocating.
tension: An active snake moving means the ground ahead is warm and undisturbed.
traveller_stance: Steps around the track's crossing-point. Continues.

npc_attitude: A large snake on the warm rock above the road — visible because the sun catches its scales and it is not moving.
concrete_content: Basking. The scale pattern is distinctive — a viper of the large southern variety, not the common small one of northern roads.
tension: It will not move unless approached or disturbed. The gap between the rock and the road verge is sufficient.
traveller_stance: Passes below the rock without approaching. The snake does not respond.

npc_attitude: A dozen lizards on the sun-warmed stones of the road-wall — small, quick, disappearing into crevices as the traveller passes.
concrete_content: Normal. They are thermally regulating. Their presence means no large predator has disturbed these stones today.
tension: Small reptiles in quantity on a sunny wall are a proxy for a calm stretch of road.
traveller_stance: Notes the calm. Continues.

npc_attitude: A snake across the path, absorbing heat. It feels the vibration before it hears anything and is gone before the traveller reaches it.
concrete_content: Not aggressive — the fastest-moving thing the traveller will encounter all day and it is using that speed to disappear.
tension: The path is clear. The snake is in the undergrowth watching.
traveller_stance: Continues without incident.

npc_attitude: Dumbledoors working the clover at the verge — large, unhurried, producing that specific sound that is halfway between a drone and a grumble.
concrete_content: Healthy meadow, no disturbance. The big bumble-bees are only this relaxed when the ground around them is undisturbed.
tension: A quiet road ahead. The bees say so.
traveller_stance: Continues.

npc_attitude: An empty nest on the road — a wasps' nest the size of a helm, freshly torn from the eave above. Recent disturbance.
concrete_content: Something pulled this nest down within the last few hours. The wasps have dispersed — most of them, not all. The stragglers are still around.
tension: Something large enough to pull down a nest this size either wanted the grubs or didn't notice it. Neither is reassuring.
traveller_stance: Gives the dispersed stragglers a wide berth. Continues.

npc_attitude: A swarm on the road — bees or wasps, moving as a single organism, crossing the road at exactly the worst moment.
concrete_content: The swarm is not aggressive. It is in transit, following its queen, completely occupied with itself. The road happens to be in the way.
tension: Waiting is the answer. Three minutes and they are gone.
traveller_stance: Stops. Waits at the road edge. Watches the swarm pass.

npc_attitude: Hummerhorns above the path — not a swarm, four or five scouts, which is the worst possible configuration: enough to alert the colony, few enough to be difficult to track.
concrete_content: They found something that disturbed them. The traveller or whatever the traveller is carrying. They are moving in the specific pattern that precedes summoning.
tension: Three minutes before the colony arrives. Two of those minutes have already passed.
traveller_stance: Moves off the path at ninety degrees. Fast. Downwind.

npc_attitude: Fireflies in the dusk meadow — hundreds of them, the cold green light rising and falling in patterns that seem almost deliberate.
concrete_content: This is normal and beautiful and means the meadow is healthy and the evening is quiet.
tension: The fireflies are the evening news: nothing alarming, air is clean, moisture is good.
traveller_stance: Watches them for a moment. Sets up camp.

npc_attitude: Fox-sign on the path — a scatter of pheasant feathers and the distinctive sharp scent. Recently, in the last hour.
concrete_content: The fox was successful. A successful hunt means an undisturbed wood. The pheasant was moving normally until it wasn't.
tension: Quiet road.
traveller_stance: Continues.

npc_attitude: Squirrels working the beech-mast beside the road — industrious, unhurried, moving up and down in the canopy with the specific busyness of autumn storage.
concrete_content: Late season behaviour. The squirrels are hurrying because the season is shortening. The nuts are ready. The year is turning.
tension: A calendar observation as much as a wildlife encounter.
traveller_stance: Notes the season in the body rather than the mind. Continues.

npc_attitude: A bear on the hillside above the road — foraging in the berry-scrub, aware of the traveller, not interested.
concrete_content: A bear that makes the choice to ignore a traveller is a bear that has made this calculation before and found travelers not worth the trouble.
tension: The indifference is a good sign. A habituated, well-fed bear in berry season is the least dangerous version of a bear encounter.
traveller_stance: Continues at the same pace. Does not make eye contact. Does not run.

npc_attitude: Something large in the undergrowth — the sound of something heavy moving away fast, the branches shaking in a retreating line.
concrete_content: It was close enough that the traveller almost walked into it. Whatever it was, it wanted no contact as much as the traveller did.
tension: The withdrawal was fast and clean. Whatever it was, it knew how to move through this undergrowth.
traveller_stance: Waits for the shaking to stop. Continues.

npc_attitude: A grey ape — huge, shaggy, five feet at the shoulder — steps onto the path ten metres ahead, sees the traveller, and immediately turns and leaves.
concrete_content: The speed of its departure is surprising for its size. It was more frightened than the traveller.
tension: Something the traveller is carrying, or the shadow the traveller carries, read as dangerous to an animal that is not easily frightened.
traveller_stance: Watches it go. Considers what it smelled.

npc_attitude: Horse-sign on the road — shod hooves, three horses, moving at a canter heading south. Made this morning.
concrete_content: Shod means riders, not wild horses. Three horses at a canter heading south means a message or a patrol moving with purpose.
tension: Three riders with a purpose, somewhere south on this road.
traveller_stance: Notes the number and direction. Continues.

npc_attitude: Wild horses on the horizon — a small band, perhaps eight, moving in the specific unhurried drift of animals with no predator pressure and nowhere they need to be.
concrete_content: Free horses in good condition mean this land is currently safe. Wolves would have thinned them or changed their behaviour.
tension: A useful read on the region.
traveller_stance: Notes the condition of the horses. Continues.

npc_attitude: A horse-herd at a water-hole — a dozen animals, mixed, the foals still close to their mothers. Unafraid of the road.
concrete_content: Habituated to road-traffic, which means this road is regularly used. Road-traffic means relative safety and commerce.
tension: Active roads are safe roads. The horses confirm it.
traveller_stance: Notes the herd's comfort. Continues.

npc_attitude: Wild horses that were grazing the road-verge scatter as the traveller rounds the bend — all moving upwind in a single line, which is the flight pattern of horses responding to something they have scented, not seen.
concrete_content: They scented the traveller before seeing them and decided the scent was wrong. Not predator-wrong — dark-wrong.
tension: Animals read the shadow differently than people do. What the horses smelled is not visible.
traveller_stance: Watches them go. Considers what they read in the scent.

npc_attitude: The marsh beside the road is loud with frogs — the full chorus of an undisturbed spring night, every pond and ditch contributing.
concrete_content: Frogs chorus when they are safe and the air is right. A full chorus means no snake or heron has disturbed this marsh in the last hour.
tension: The marsh is clean and safe. The frogs are saying so loudly.
traveller_stance: Notes the chorus. Uses the noise as a cover for their own movement.

npc_attitude: Toads on the road in the rain — dozens of them, moving in the same direction with the specific purposefulness of migration.
concrete_content: Toad migration on a wet night means the road will be slow and careful or it will involve a great deal of accidental toad-murder.
tension: The toads have priorities. The traveller is not among them.
traveller_stance: Picks a way through without stopping. The toads ignore them.

npc_attitude: The ford is active with frogs — thousands of them, breeding in the shallows, the water barely visible through the mass of movement.
concrete_content: Not dangerous. Deeply unpleasant to wade through. The frogs will be done in three days.
tension: The ford is technically passable. Three days would be better.
traveller_stance: Considers the three-day wait against the alternative. Wades.

npc_attitude: A woman at a farmstead gate — she stops what she is doing when the traveller passes, neither welcoming nor unwelcoming.
concrete_content: She asks which road the traveller came from — not curiosity, she is waiting for someone from that direction and the traveller is not them.
tension: She will not say who she is waiting for. The question is whether the traveller saw anyone on the road behind them.
traveller_stance: Names the road. Describes who was on it. Lets her draw her own conclusions.

npc_attitude: A man on the road moving fast in the opposite direction — he slows when he sees the traveller, just enough to exchange a word.
concrete_content: He says the eastern garrison road is being watched — not by soldiers, by something else, and he cannot say more clearly than that. He does not stop.
tension: He is frightened enough to keep moving but not so frightened he said nothing.
traveller_stance: Notes what he could not say clearly. Takes the western road.

npc_attitude: A group of three at a wayhouse fire — Gondorian by their dress, quiet in the way of people who have been quiet for several days.
concrete_content: They came from Minas Tirith three weeks ago on a courier errand. The errand is done. They are not going back yet, which they will not explain.
tension: Three Gondorian couriers who have finished their errand and are not returning is an unusual configuration.
traveller_stance: Sits at the same fire. Does not ask the question directly.

npc_attitude: A horseman who has dismounted to check a shoe — he raises a hand when the traveller passes, the universal greeting of someone with their hands occupied.
concrete_content: He asks if the traveller saw any wolf-sign on the southern road. His flock was hit two nights ago and the track led that way.
tension: A single wolf taking from a flock is normal. A wolf that moves south after is unusual.
traveller_stance: Tells him what the southern road looked like.

npc_attitude: Two of them at a ford — they check the traveller with a quick professional assessment that is not unfriendly, just thorough.
concrete_content: They are running a circuit for a local lord and they want to know what the road east looks like. They share: the road west had fresh Orc-sign two days ago, above the tree-line.
tension: Orc-sign above the tree-line means scouts, not raiders. Scouts report back.
traveller_stance: Trades road information. Takes the Orc-sign.

npc_attitude: A lone rider on the road, moving at a walk, which is wrong — a Northman on a road at this hour should be moving faster.
concrete_content: His horse is tired and so is he and he has been riding for two days with minimal sleep. He is carrying something he will not describe, to someone he will not name, and he needs to know if the road ahead is clear.
tension: The urgency and the secrecy are both real. What he is carrying is important enough to exhaust both horse and rider.
traveller_stance: Tells him what the road ahead looks like. Does not ask what he is carrying.

npc_attitude: A man on the road with the particular self-contained manner of someone who has been walking alone for a long time and has stopped expecting company.
concrete_content: He is going to Bree. He has been going to Bree for eleven days, which means he started from somewhere far enough north that few people go there voluntarily.
tension: Men coming south from the deep north are either Rangers, refugees, or carrying information. He does not look like a refugee.
traveller_stance: Asks where north he started from. Gets a careful, partial answer.

npc_attitude: A woman at a crossroads, reading a posted notice nailed to the waypost. She looks up when the traveller arrives.
concrete_content: The notice is a missing-person notice — a man, forty years, last seen on the Weather Hills road three weeks ago. She says she knew him. She says this in the past tense before catching herself.
tension: The past tense is involuntary. She already knows he is dead. The question is how she knows.
traveller_stance: Reads the notice. Asks if she filed it.

npc_attitude: He steps out of cover — not threateningly, but he was in cover and now he is not, which is its own message.
concrete_content: He is a Ranger running a circuit that should have had three men. The other two have not reported back in six days. He is continuing the circuit alone because the circuit must be run, not because it is a good idea.
tension: A Ranger continuing a three-man circuit alone, on day six of silence from his partners, is a man running on duty and not much else.
traveller_stance: Tells him what the road has looked like. Asks if he wants company for the northern section.

npc_attitude: A clan-man on the road with a pack-load of something he is not advertising. He eyes the traveller steadily.
concrete_content: He is moving between clan-holds and he has business that is his own. He will trade road-news but nothing else.
tension: The pack is heavy and he is not making detours. Whatever he is carrying, the destination is specific.
traveller_stance: Trades road-news. Does not ask about the pack.

npc_attitude: Two of them at a fire off the road, who watch the traveller approach without invitation or hostility.
concrete_content: They let the traveller come to the fire because the night is cold and they are Dunlendings, not animals. One of them speaks enough Westron to communicate. He says the road north of the river is being watched by men he does not recognise.
tension: Men watching roads who the Dunlendings do not recognise are a category worth paying attention to.
traveller_stance: Asks what manner of men. Gets a description that is sparse but accurate.

npc_attitude: A woman on the road — elderly, moving with the specific deliberate pace of someone who does not hurry because she has not needed to hurry in a long time.
concrete_content: She is a clan-healer making a circuit of the outlying steadings. She looks at the traveller with the diagnostic attention of her profession and says: you have been carrying something heavy for a long time.
tension: She means the shadow, not the pack. She does not know the word shadow but she can read its signs.
traveller_stance: Agrees that yes, the road has been long.

npc_attitude: A sailor off a river-boat, killing time at a wayhouse while the boat is loaded. He is relaxed and conversational in the way of men who spend most of their time in small spaces with the same people.
concrete_content: He has been running the river between Pelargir and Harlond for twelve years and he knows every sandbar and garrison and toll-point on it. He will tell you anything you want to know about the river in exchange for news from inland.
tension: He has not been inland in months. He is genuinely curious.
traveller_stance: Trades inland news for river news. Gets more than was given.

npc_attitude: A man at the harbour-side who looks at the traveller for a moment too long before looking away.
concrete_content: He is watching for someone. The description he was given is close enough to the traveller that he checked, then ruled it out. He relaxes fractionally.
tension: Someone is being looked for on this waterfront. The traveller almost matched the description.
traveller_stance: Notes the look and the relaxation. Files the encounter.

npc_attitude: A tribesman on the high path, carrying game — he stops when he sees the traveller and waits to see what happens next.
concrete_content: He does not speak Westron well but the gesture language of the road is universal. He shows the road ahead: one finger, then a horizontal gesture, then both hands moving apart. One road, a split, choose.
tension: He knows which fork to take. He is deciding whether to share that with an outsider.
traveller_stance: Waits. Does not press. Lets him decide.

npc_attitude: A mountain-man at a spring, filling a skin. He looks up without alarm — he heard the traveller long before they arrived.
concrete_content: He says, in accented but serviceable Westron, that the pass ahead had fresh rockfall three days ago. Still passable, but one section is unstable and loud — anything large moving under it risks more fall.
tension: He chose to pass this on. Mountain-folk do not waste words on strangers without reason.
traveller_stance: Asks if there is a way around the unstable section.

npc_attitude: A garrison soldier at a checkpoint — bored, following procedure, not hostile.
concrete_content: He checks for papers. The check is real — he records what he finds in a ledger. He does not explain what the ledger is for.
tension: The ledger is the problem. The information in it goes somewhere.
traveller_stance: Provides what is required. Notes the ledger.

npc_attitude: He comes out of a building alone to intercept the traveller before they reach the main road. This was coordinated.
concrete_content: He says: someone wants to speak with you. He says it in a tone that makes clear the want is not a request. He does not say who.
tension: The coordination means the traveller was identified before they arrived here. The route was anticipated.
traveller_stance: Asks who. Gets a title, not a name.

npc_attitude: A knot of villagers at a well — they go quiet when the traveller approaches, then resume when the traveller is obviously not a threat.
concrete_content: One of them, bolder than the rest, asks where the traveller is coming from. The question carries the specific anxiety of people waiting for news from a direction they are watching.
tension: They are waiting for something. The traveller is not it, but might know something about it.
traveller_stance: Names the road. Gives the road-news. Watches the anxiety resolve or deepen.

npc_attitude: A woman drawing water who looks at the traveller with the frank assessment of someone who has seen enough travelers to read them quickly.
concrete_content: She says the village headman wants to speak with anyone coming off the northern road. She says this without urgency — it is a standing request, not an emergency.
tension: A standing request means it has been standing for some time. Something on the northern road is being tracked through traveler reports.
traveller_stance: Asks if this is about a specific event or a general watch.

npc_attitude: A group outside a farmhouse who watch the traveller pass with the still attention of people who have been told to watch.
concrete_content: One of them calls out: which road did you come from? They want to know if the traveller saw anything on the road that would explain the smoke column visible to the north this morning.
tension: Smoke to the north that nobody can explain and a village watching the road with attention is a village that already suspects something.
traveller_stance: Tells them what the northern road looked like.

npc_attitude: Four soldiers on the road — not blocking it, standing at the side in the manner of a patrol that has stopped to check something.
concrete_content: The sergeant asks the traveller for the road they came from and anything notable they saw. The question is standard patrol procedure, delivered without threat.
tension: The procedure is real and the sergeant is competent. The answer will be recorded and reported.
traveller_stance: Gives the honest road report. Notes what they are specifically interested in.

npc_attitude: A patrol at a crossroads — six, in reasonable order, the sergeant studying a section of the road with more attention than the road warrants.
concrete_content: They are tracking something on this road. The sergeant looks up, assesses the traveller in two seconds, and asks: how long ago did you pass through the valley?
tension: They are following a trail. The traveller may have been on the same road as whatever left it.
traveller_stance: Names the time. Describes what was on the road. Lets the sergeant connect what he connects.

npc_attitude: A patrol blocking the road — not aggressively, but completely. The sergeant comes forward alone.
concrete_content: The road is closed ahead. He says this once, clearly, without explanation. He is following orders he may not have been given the full reason for.
tension: A road closure with no explanation means the reason is either classified or unknown to the sergeant himself.
traveller_stance: Asks when it will reopen. The sergeant does not know.

npc_attitude: A patrol that has identified the traveller as a specific subject of interest — the formation changes when they see them.
concrete_content: The sergeant has a description. He reads it off a written order. The description matches closely enough that he is obligated to detain the traveller for questioning.
tension: The sergeant is not hostile — he is following procedure. The procedure may lead somewhere the traveller does not want to go.
traveller_stance: Does not run. Asks to read the order.

npc_attitude: Eight of them, and the sergeant has sent two around the back of the traveller before speaking. This was planned.
concrete_content: They are looking for someone specific. The traveller is the closest match they have found. The sergeant is professional enough to want confirmation before acting.
tension: The question that confirms or denies will come. The answer determines what happens next.
traveller_stance: Answers the confirmation question honestly. Watches the sergeant decide.

npc_attitude: Boot-prints on the road — military-pattern boots, six sets, moving in loose formation heading east. Made this morning.
concrete_content: A patrol heading east at dawn on this road. Their spacing is correct and their stride is even. A disciplined patrol on a purpose.
tension: The purpose that takes a disciplined patrol east on this road at dawn is worth knowing.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction and discipline. Continues.

npc_attitude: A patrol visible on the ridge above the road — moving parallel, watching the road below without interacting with it.
concrete_content: They are not on the road. They are above it, watching it. This is either overwatch for something on the road or they are watching for something they expect to come down from above.
tension: Patrols above roads watch the road. What they are watching for is the question.
traveller_stance: Continues on the road. Does not look up for more than a glance.

npc_attitude: Three of them on the road — armed, watching. The one in front has the bearing of someone who has been appointed to speak.
concrete_content: He asks what the traveller is carrying and where they are going. The question is territorial — this is Dunlending land and he is exercising that fact, not starting a robbery.
tension: The distinction between a territorial question and a robbery depends entirely on the answer.
traveller_stance: Names the destination. Names the load honestly.

npc_attitude: A small group at the road's edge — Easterlings, by their dress and gear, far enough west that they are watching every approach carefully.
concrete_content: One of them speaks rough Westron. He wants to know which power holds this road — who patrols it, whose authority it answers to. He is asking because he does not yet know, and he needs to.
tension: An Easterling far west of his usual range who does not know who holds the road is either a scout, a refugee, or both.
traveller_stance: Names the nominal authority on this road. Watches how he receives it.

npc_attitude: A man on the road who adjusts his route to intersect the traveller's in a way that looks accidental and isn't.
concrete_content: He asks, conversationally, if the traveller saw any patrol activity in the last valley. He phrases it as casual curiosity. It is not.
tension: He is checking whether the road behind the traveller is clear. The reason he needs it clear is not stated.
traveller_stance: Names what was on the road behind. Does not ask why he wants to know.

npc_attitude: One of them, separated from a larger group, on the road with the easy manner of someone who has decided that appearing dangerous is more useful than being dangerous right now.
concrete_content: He asks if the traveller needs a boat. He says it like an ordinary commercial offer. He has a boat, the boat is going south, and he has room.
tension: A Corsair offering a boat to a stranger on a road is offering something, but it may not be transportation.
traveller_stance: Declines politely. Watches which way he goes to report back.

npc_attitude: Two of them at a wayhouse who make room at the fire without being asked and without warmth — the courtesy of people who follow rules about hospitality even when they do not feel them.
concrete_content: One of them says, unprompted, that the eastern road is closed three days out. He says it as information, not as a warning. The distinction is deliberate.
tension: Variags do not share information without reason. The reason here is not stated.
traveller_stance: Thanks him. Asks what is on the eastern road.

npc_attitude: One of them on the road alone — unusual, since they generally move in pairs at minimum. He looks at the traveller with the assessment of someone deciding whether to be bothered.
concrete_content: He says he is looking for someone. He describes that person in enough detail to be deliberate — the description is a message to anyone who knows the person described.
tension: The description may or may not match someone the traveller knows. If it does, the message is clear. If it doesn't, it is still a warning about what is being hunted on this road.
traveller_stance: Listens to the description. Gives nothing away.

npc_attitude: A small Sagath party who intercept the traveller at a ford — not aggressively, using the ford as a natural chokepoint for a conversation.
concrete_content: Their leader asks where the traveller is going and whether they have seen Gondorian military movements on the road. The question is intelligence-gathering and they are not being subtle about it.
tension: They are collecting information about Gondorian movements. They are doing it in the open, which means they are either very confident or very visible for a reason.
traveller_stance: Names the destination. Describes the road honestly without counting soldiers.

npc_attitude: One of them on the road inland, out of context — sailors have a way of carrying the sea with them that makes them visible on land roads.
concrete_content: He is looking for a specific inn and is comprehensively lost. The combination of competence at sea and helplessness on land is genuine and oddly disarming.
tension: A pirate lost on a road is still a pirate. The helplessness may or may not be the whole story.
traveller_stance: Gives him directions. Notes which direction he was actually heading before asking.

npc_attitude: A man on the road who greets the traveller with easy friendliness — too easy, the kind that is practised.
concrete_content: He is running a quick read of the traveller: what are they carrying, where are they going, are they alone, what are they worth. The conversation is the read.
tension: He is deciding. The decision is not yet made.
traveller_stance: Gives nothing useful. Keeps moving.

npc_attitude: One of them on the path — visible, which is unusual. He is watching the traveller directly.
concrete_content: He says, in rough Westron: you are going wrong way. He does not elaborate. He points, once, in another direction.
tension: The Woses know this forest better than anyone. If he says the way is wrong, the way is wrong.
traveller_stance: Asks what is wrong about it.

npc_attitude: Two of them appear from the undergrowth at the forest edge — not threateningly, but without any attempt at subtlety either.
concrete_content: One of them holds up three fingers, then points down the road, then makes a slow closing gesture with his hand. Three of something on the road ahead, waiting.
tension: He chose to warn the traveller. That is not nothing from a Wose.
traveller_stance: Asks with gestures: what kind of three?

npc_attitude: It comes around the bend in the road already moving — no warning, no posture, simply in motion toward the traveller.
concrete_content: A Hill-troll, running. The stride covers eight feet. It is not angry — it is hungry, which is more dangerous because hunger has no off-switch.
tension: Fifteen seconds to impact at this closing speed. The road has no cover on either side.
traveller_stance: Moves off the road. Does not run on it.

npc_attitude: Three of them, from three directions simultaneously. This is not coincidence.
concrete_content: Stone-trolls coordinating an ambush means someone organized them, or they have done this before and learned. The three directions close all obvious exits.
tension: Three Stone-trolls who understand tactics are qualitatively different from three Stone-trolls who argue about cooking.
traveller_stance: Does not freeze. Identifies the weakest corner. Moves toward it.

npc_attitude: An arrow from the treeline — not a miss, a ranging shot, telling the traveller that they are within range and the orcs know it.
concrete_content: A ranging shot before the attack means they want the traveller to stop, which means they want the traveller alive. That is both better and worse than a kill-shot.
tension: The next shot will not be a ranging shot.
traveller_stance: Does not stop. Does not run straight. Moves toward the nearest cover at an angle.

npc_attitude: They come out of the dark on both sides of the road — too many to count quickly, too coordinated to be a random patrol.
concrete_content: This is an ambush set specifically for this road at this time. Someone told them the traveller would be here.
tension: The ambush was prepared. That means information was passed. The traveller was tracked or betrayed before this road.
traveller_stance: Does not think about the implications now. Survives first.

npc_attitude: It does not approach — it is simply closer than it was, without having moved in any observable way.
concrete_content: Barrow-wights do not chase. They close distance in the moments when the prey blinks or looks away. The gap between them is now half what it was.
tension: Looking at it directly does not stop it. Not looking at it is worse.
traveller_stance: Keeps it in sight. Moves toward open ground where the air is different.

npc_attitude: A strand of web across the path that was not there a moment ago — anchor-line, thicker than a finger, at throat height.
concrete_content: The web appeared because something moved above the canopy to place it. The spider is above, not on the ground. The anchor-line is not a trap — it is the beginning of one.
tension: Two seconds before the next strand drops.
traveller_stance: Ducks under it. Runs. Does not look up.

npc_attitude: The path behind is sealed. At some point while moving forward, the way back became web — strong, anchored, impassable without a blade.
concrete_content: This was done quietly while the traveller was watching ahead. The spider — or spiders — sealed the retreat first, which means they intend to take their time.
tension: The way back requires cutting through. The way forward may be equally closed by now.
traveller_stance: Does not attempt to cut through. Cuts at an angle toward the least-dense section of the forest.

npc_attitude: The temperature drops ten degrees in two steps — not weather, localized, wrong. The darkness ahead is darker than the darkness behind.
concrete_content: Something is standing in the path. It is not visible so much as the absence of everything else — light bends around it, sound drops out, the air pressure changes.
tension: Running is the wrong answer. Running is what it expects.
traveller_stance: Stops. Does not look at it directly. Identifies the strongest light source available and moves toward it.

npc_attitude: The ford feels different underfoot — the bottom that was firm on the first step is shifting on the second.
concrete_content: Something below the surface has changed the bottom. The ford is being unmade from underneath while the traveller is crossing it.
tension: The centre of the ford is now above whatever is moving below. The banks are twenty feet in either direction.
traveller_stance: Does not stop moving. Reaches the bank before the shift completes.

npc_attitude: An arm from the water — wrong proportion, too many joints, too long — closing around the nearest ankle.
concrete_content: The Vodyanoi does not surface. It reaches from depth. The grip is cold and strong and it is already pulling.
tension: The water is its element. The bank is three steps away.
traveller_stance: Drives the nearest hard object into the grip. Makes the three steps.

npc_attitude: No warning. It was on the rock above and now it is not, and the shadow passes over before the sound of the wings reaches the ground.
concrete_content: A drake stooping from height covers the distance in under two seconds. The first pass is a grab-and-rake, not a breath-weapon — it wants to assess what it has before committing to more.
tension: The first pass determines whether there is a second.
traveller_stance: Moves perpendicular to the approach vector on the first pass.

npc_attitude: It is closer than it was. This is the only way to describe what happened — nothing was observed, no movement was registered, it is simply closer.
concrete_content: A barrow-wight or bound ghost closing distance is not moving in any physical sense. It is the distance that changes, not the entity. This makes it deeply difficult to respond to conventionally.
tension: Looking away is the mechanism. Keeping it in continuous sight may not be possible.
traveller_stance: Does not look away. Does not blink. Moves toward the nearest threshold — a door, a crossroads, running water.

npc_attitude: It has been following for three hours. Not approaching — following. The distance has been constant. Until ten minutes ago.
concrete_content: Whatever changed ten minutes ago, the undead thing behind the traveller felt it and acted on it. Shadow rising, energy falling, the traveller weakening in some way that the dead can read.
tension: It has been patient for three hours. Its patience has run out.
traveller_stance: Does not run. Running is its preferred prey-state. Stops and faces it.

npc_attitude: The barrow is sealed. There is nothing visible. But the air near it costs something to breathe — not physically, in another sense that has no precise name.
concrete_content: Barrows sealed by Dúnedain ward-work do not leak. This one is leaking. Whatever is inside is old and the warding has weakened.
tension: The leaking is recent. The warding held for decades before now.
traveller_stance: Does not stop near the barrow. Increases distance from it. Notes it for whoever should know.

npc_attitude: The Nazgûl does not pass close enough to be seen. But the shadow it casts moves ahead of it, and the shadow reaches the traveller before the Nazgûl does.
concrete_content: A cold that is not temperature, a silence that is not quiet, and then the shadow — moving against the light, independent of the source, touching everything it passes over.
tension: The shadow notices what is in it. The traveller is in it.
traveller_stance: Does not move. Does not draw attention. Waits for the shadow to pass.

npc_attitude: A snapped tree beside the road — not wind-snapped, the break is clean and the trunk has been moved, not fallen.
concrete_content: Something used this tree as a handhold or a lever. The size of the break and the displacement suggest something very heavy moving through here in the dark.
tension: The tree was healthy. Whatever broke it did so without effort.
traveller_stance: Notes the break-height. Notes the direction of travel. Continues.

npc_attitude: From the valley — the sound of large rocks being moved. Not rockfall. Deliberate.
concrete_content: Trolls stack rocks. Hunting caches, territory markers, the beginning of crude shelters. The activity is purposeful. There is at least one of them in that valley doing something intentional.
tension: The valley is between the traveller and the next road section.
traveller_stance: Waits until the sound stops. Gives it another ten minutes. Takes the ridge route.

npc_attitude: On the hillside above the road at dusk — a shape too large for any man, moving with the slow certainty of something that does not expect to be challenged.
concrete_content: A Stone-troll on open ground in the last light before dark. It is going somewhere specific — the stride is purposeful. The road below it is where the traveller is standing.
tension: Trolls are active at night. Dusk is the beginning of their day.
traveller_stance: Moves off the road before the light fails. Camps away from the road.

npc_attitude: Drums, distant — the specific rhythm of Orc military communication, not celebration.
concrete_content: The rhythm is a signal, not music. It repeats four times, stops, resumes. A call-and-confirm pattern. Someone sent a message and someone confirmed receipt.
tension: Military drum communication means organized forces. Organized forces on this road means they know the road.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction. Counts the repetitions. Adjusts the route.

npc_attitude: A patrol visible on the far ridge — dark shapes against the sky, moving in single file. Counted: eight.
concrete_content: Eight Orcs on a ridge at midday means either they are confident this ground belongs to them or they are moving fast enough that concealment is secondary to speed.
tension: Eight Orcs moving confidently on a ridge in daylight is a message about who controls this ground.
traveller_stance: Does not skyline. Stays in the valley-bottom until the patrol is out of sight.

npc_attitude: The sign has been there for an hour — the same set of prints, keeping pace. Not running, not closing, just there.
concrete_content: One Orc tracking a traveller without closing is a scout, not a raider. It is maintaining contact and reporting position.
tension: Somewhere ahead of or behind the traveller, the scout's information is being received.
traveller_stance: Changes route unpredictably. Tests whether the shadow follows the change.

npc_attitude: A howl — not nearby, a mile or two, but answered within seconds from a different direction.
concrete_content: Call and response. Two wolves at minimum, coordinating. The calls establish position relative to something — probably the traveller on this open road.
tension: Wolves that call to each other about a moving target are hunting it. The calls were honest about the direction.
traveller_stance: Moves toward the nearest cover. Builds the fire larger than usual tonight.

npc_attitude: A wolf on the ridge above the road — visible because it is sitting and watching, not because it moved.
concrete_content: It has been there for some time. It registered the traveller's approach far enough back that it was already settled when the traveller came into view.
tension: A single wolf watching a road from a ridge is either a scout or an individual with a territory claim on this road.
traveller_stance: Notes it. Does not stop. Keeps moving.

npc_attitude: A wolf in the road ahead — it sees the traveller and leaves. Not flees, leaves. At a steady trot toward the treeline.
concrete_content: A wolf that chooses to leave rather than test an encounter has made a calculation about the outcome. The calculation went in the traveller's favour.
tension: The wolf went into the trees. It did not go over the ridge.
traveller_stance: Notes which side of the road it entered. Continues without relaxing.

npc_attitude: A shape in the canopy above the path — not a bird, moving too deliberately, from branch to branch without sound.
concrete_content: An Elf moving through the canopy in the direction the traveller is heading. Not following — preceding. Moving ahead on a parallel path.
tension: Elves who move ahead of travelers on their roads are either escorting them or evaluating them. The distinction becomes clear when they stop.
traveller_stance: Continues on the path. Does not look up again.

npc_attitude: At the forest edge, for a moment — standing, watching the road, then gone between one blink and the next.
concrete_content: A Silvan Elf at the wood's edge is either a border-watcher or someone who came to look at something specific on the road. The watching was deliberate and the departure was deliberate.
tension: It saw what it came to see. The traveller may or may not be what it was looking for.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction it faced. Notes where it was standing on the boundary.

npc_attitude: The forest is being watched. Not the traveller specifically — the whole section of road. From multiple points.
concrete_content: Silvan border-watch. Three separate positions visible only because the light shifted. They have been watching this road for some time and they are watching it now.
tension: The watch means the forest has reason to watch this particular road at this particular time.
traveller_stance: Continues on the road. Does not enter the forest.

npc_attitude: Survey marks cut into the rock face above the road — fresh chisel-work, specific angles and depths that are not decorative.
concrete_content: Dwarven survey-marks mean a Dwarven survey team has been through this area recently. The marks will tell a Dwarven geologist about the rock composition and the depth of a potential shaft. They are probably still in the area.
tension: Survey teams precede mining operations. Mining operations change roads.
traveller_stance: Notes the marks. Continues.

npc_attitude: A Dwarven caravan on the road ahead — four ponies, two wagons, moving at the pace of heavily loaded animals.
concrete_content: Trade goods heading somewhere with value. The escort is three Dwarves visible, probably more not visible. They are not going to be robbed and they know it.
tension: Heavily loaded Dwarven caravans move on roads they consider safe. Their presence is its own assessment of the route.
traveller_stance: Passes them with a nod. Notes what the road looks like to creatures who have been on it longer today.

npc_attitude: A Dwarven camp off the road — organized, fires banked, the tools and equipment of a working party rather than travelers.
concrete_content: They are doing something in this location deliberately — surveying, mining, repairing a structure, or marking territory. The equipment determines which.
tension: Dwarves working in a specific location have a purpose for that location. The purpose shapes how they will respond to the traveller.
traveller_stance: Approaches openly. Does not enter the camp without invitation.

npc_attitude: The birds are behaving strangely — not frightened, organized. Moving in a specific direction in species-groups, as if something has asked them to.
concrete_content: Radagast moves through this region periodically and the creatures know it. What the traveller is seeing is the aftermath of a Maia's passage — the wood responding to him.
tension: He was here recently. He may have left for a reason or he may return.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction the birds are moving. Considers whether to follow the same direction.

npc_attitude: A column of smoke from the forest — too deliberate to be accidental, too large to be a campfire.
concrete_content: A Maia signal, or something a Maia is watching, or the remnant of a Maia's working. The smoke has a colour that is not entirely consistent with any fuel that should be burning there.
tension: Smoke of that colour in a forest that should not be burning means something is being done here that has consequences.
traveller_stance: Does not approach the smoke. Notes its direction and the approximate time.

npc_attitude: An ancient tree at the road's edge — larger than any tree nearby, different species, with a presence that makes the traveller slow without knowing why.
concrete_content: Not an Ent. A tree that has been here long enough to accumulate something that the younger trees around it lack — not consciousness, exactly, but age that has become weight.
tension: Nothing here is dangerous. But this tree has been at this crossroads for longer than the road has existed.
traveller_stance: Passes it with the particular care that old things deserve.

npc_attitude: The trees in this section of the forest are oriented differently — their main branches face the road in a way that is not sun-seeking.
concrete_content: This section of the forest has been awake for some time. Not hostile, not welcoming. Attentive. Something on this road has been worth watching recently.
tension: A forest that is paying attention is a forest that has a reason to pay attention.
traveller_stance: Moves through without stopping. Does not break anything.

npc_attitude: A sound from the trees — not wind, not animal. Slow, low, resonant. Like language at a frequency just below comprehension.
concrete_content: The trees are talking to each other. The subject is the traveller, most likely, or what the traveller carries, or what the traveller represents to something that is also in this forest.
tension: The communication is ongoing. The topic has not been resolved.
traveller_stance: Does not stop. Does not answer. Keeps moving through.

npc_attitude: A Hobbit visible at the top of a hill above the road — distinctive silhouette, standing and watching the traveller pass.
concrete_content: They are curious. They are always curious. This one has climbed a hill specifically to get a better view of the road, which is more initiative than most people show.
tension: The watching is benign. It is the watching of someone who will describe this to seven people tonight.
traveller_stance: Returns the look. Continues.

npc_attitude: Hobbit-feet in the mud at the road's edge — unmistakeable, large and hairy and bare-soled. Two sets, heading toward the village.
concrete_content: They walked here recently, at a comfortable pace, and they were carrying something — the depth of the prints suggests a full pack. Moving toward home at the end of the day.
tension: Nothing threatening here. The Shire is close, or a Hobbit community is.
traveller_stance: Notes the direction. If the road leads that way, good hospitality may follow.
